title: Czech false friends (B1)
note: Words that look Czech and are not. The whole unit is L1 interference, so every item shows the wrong meaning next to the right one. First draft 2026-09-02. · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: sentences 8 → 36, one gappable frame per lemma. The tiles carry their sense in parentheses and lemmaBare strips it, so every frame gaps the bare word. E10: Use is use_mode rewrite, 12 items — and on this pack the paraphrase IS the trap: *real* → actual, *understanding* → sympathetic, *in the end* → eventually. · E4: **concurrence** was tiled with the gloss *(rare)* — the pack itself admitting nobody says it. Replaced with **artist** (umělec, NE artista = acrobat), which is a false friend a Czech learner actually trips on. · F7 does not bite here: nearly every tile is a word taught elsewhere, and that is the point of the unit; each one carries its sense in parentheses, which is the A12 mark. · Pool-checked against everything taught before leaf_false_friends_b1 — 0 unknown types.

intro.note: These words look like Czech words and mean something else. The Czech meaning always has a different English word — those are on the last page.
